source: AAA gasprices.aaa.com national average — June 1, 2026 (Day 94) $4.322, easing from the May 29 (Day 91) print of $4.391 as the late-May crude pullback (Brent's worst month since 2020, down >19%) fed through to the pump and ceasefire-extension optimism persisted. Highest states: Hawaii $5.634, Washington DC $4.596. Still ~+45% above the $2.99 Feb 28 baseline and ~29¢ below the June 2022 all-time record of $4.61, even after Brent rebounded to settle $94.98 on June 1 on renewed conflict fears. Watson Institute / Costs of War (Brown — Jeff Colgan, May 18 brief): cumulative extra fuel costs to U.S. consumers since the war began top $40 billion, more than $300 per household. ITEP tracker (May 31): average additional cost per U.S. household $347.72; cumulative ~$46.5 billion paid extra to the oil industry since Feb 28; summer-end forecast $825.02/household. Patrick De Haan (GasBuddy): pump-price relief runs 2-3 weeks behind crude.
